Subject: Technical note: initial root-cause signal + recommended rollback

Quick technical update from infra analysis:
- Signal: we are seeing a spike in KV cache evictions on the model-serving layer coincident with a rolling deploy that started at 08:58 PDT. Cache churn caused a large increase in cold KV lookups and longer decode paths, amplifying CPU/GPU time per request. That, combined with a small surge in request concurrency from FastPay between 09:00–09:07, pushed the serving pool into queueing/backpressure and generated 5xx responses.
- Recommendation (immediate): revert the 08:58 rolling deploy to previous variant (deploy-20260920-1100) and pin FastPay to the warmed variant for 60 minutes. On rollback we should see drop in tail latency within 6–12 minutes.
- Telemetry to watch: per-tenant KV hit-rate (dashboard link), per-instance GPU queue length, and 5xx by route.

I've attached runbook steps (runbook-rollback-variant.txt) with exact commands and safety checks. Ben — please coordinate the rollback window and the capacity pin.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
